claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy with several principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios.
The starting catalyst has a low platinum-group-metal content.
A mild post-synthesis oxidation treatment will cause cerium to migrate selectively to the alloy surface.
Surface-segregated cerium will oxidize to form a nanometer-scale CeO2 overlayer.
The ceria overlayer will enhance local redox properties by providing active oxygen species.
The ceria overlayer will act as a durable barrier to catalyst sintering.
The ceria overlayer will protect the fine alloy microstructure from degradation.
Suppressing sintering and degradation will preserve catalytic activity under cycling conditions.
The treated catalyst will have higher catalytic activity than the untreated catalyst under transient, low-temperature exhaust conditions containing H2O and NO.
The treated catalyst will retain activity for longer than the untreated catalyst during thermal aging or mileage accumulation.
The treatment will improve performance without increasing platinum-group-metal consumption.
The untreated alloy loses activity because of surface degradation and sintering under the stated operating conditions.
Treatment efficacy depends on oxidation temperature, duration, and oxidation level.
Excessive oxidation may cause bulk phase transformations or catalyst deactivation.
The intervention requires sufficient initial cerium content and controlled cerium segregation.
